'''''Quercus alnifolia''''', commonly known as the '''golden oak''', is an evergreen [[oak]] species of [[Cyprus]]. Its common English name refers to the golden coloured lower surface of its leaves. ''Quercus alnifolia'' belongs to the endemic flora of the island and it is confined to the igneous geological complex of the [[Troodos Mountains]]. In February 2006, the [[parliament of Cyprus]] selected the golden oak to be the country's national tree.<ref>{{cite news | first=Leo | last=Leonidou | title=A flower for Cyprus | date= February 3, 2006 | url =http://www.cyprus-mail.com/news/main.php?id=24156&archive=1 | work =[[Cyprus Mail]] | access-date = 2007-12-30 }} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>

== Description ==

The golden oak is a much branched [[evergreen]] shrub or small tree up to {{cvt|10|m}} high. Due to its short stature (in relation to other oaks) it is sometimes referred to as the ''dwarf oak''.<ref>{{cite book | last = Ashmore | first = Wendy |author2=Arthur Bernard Knapp  | title = Archaeologies of Landscape: Contemporary Perspectives | publisher = Blackwell | year = 1999 | page = 237 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=c5UKFk47EfYC&q=%22Quercus+alnifolia%22&pg=PA237 | isbn = 0-631-21106-3}}</ref>

Its [[leaves]] are simple, obovate to suborbicular, {{cvt|1.5|–|8|cm}} long, {{cvt|1|–|7|cm}} wide, [[glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]] and shining dark green above and densely golden or brownish [[tomentose]] below, with serrate margins and raised nervation. The [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]s are strong, {{cvt|6|–|11|mm}} long and pilose. The flowers are unisexual; the male catkins are greenish-yellow forming spreading or pendulous clusters at the tips of the branches; the female flowers are [[Axillary bud|axillary]], solitary or in groups of two to three. The acorns are narrowly [[obovate]] or subcylindrical, usually tapering towards the base, {{cvt|2|–|2.5|cm}} long and {{cvt|0.8|–|1.2|cm}} wide, with a woody endocarp and cupule with strongly recurved scales.<ref>{{cite book | last = Meikle | first = R.D. | title = Flora of Cyprus | publisher = Bentham Moxon Trust | year = 1985 | location = London | pages = 1481–1482 | isbn = 0-9504876-3-5 }}</ref>

== Taxonomy==
[[File:Golden oak2.JPG|thumb|left|A golden oak shrub in a pine stand near Karvounas, [[Troodos Mountains]]]]
''Quercus alnifolia'' belongs to subgenus ''Cerris'', [[Quercus sect. Ilex|section ''Ilex'']], as with much of the mediterranean evergreen oak species.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Denk |first1=Thomas |last2=Grimm |first2=Guido W. |last3=Manos |first3=Paul S. |last4=Deng |first4=Min |last5=Hipp |first5=Andrew L. |date=2017 |title=Appendix 2.1: An updated infrageneric classification of the oaks |website=figshare |doi=10.6084/m9.figshare.5547622.v1 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Appendix_2_1_________An_updated_infrageneric_classification_of_the_oaks/5547622/1 |access-date=2023-02-18 |format=xls |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> Occasional hybridization with [[Quercus coccifera|kermes oak]] (''Quercus coccifera'') has been described.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Neophytou |first=Ch. |author2=Palli G. |author3=Aravanopoulos F.A. |year=2007 |title=Morphological differentiation and hybridization between ''Quercus alnifolia'' Poech and ''Quercus coccifera'' L. (Fagaceae) in Cyprus |journal=Silvae Genetica |volume=56 |issue=6 |pages=271–277 |doi=10.1515/sg-2007-0038 |doi-access=free |s2cid=91154432}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==

''Quercus alnifolia'' is restricted to Troodos Massif, where it grows on [[igneous]] geological substrate at elevations of {{Convert|400 to 1800|m|abbr=on}}.<ref>{{cite book | last = Merlo | first = Maurizio | title = Valuing Mediterranean Forests: Towards Total Economic Value | publisher = CABI Publishing | year = 2005 | page = 217 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=gQ4XcwOZ-YYC&q=%22Quercus+alnifolia%22&pg=PA217 | isbn = 0-85199-480-6 }}</ref> It occupies dry habitats in association with ''[[Pinus brutia]]'' or forms dense maquis in mesic habitats, characterized by deep forest soils.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Barbéro  |first=M. |author2=Quézel P.  |year=1979 |title= Contribution à l' étude des groupements forestiers de Chypre |journal= Documents Phytosociologiques |issue=IV |pages=9–34 }}</ref>

== Ecology ==

Golden oak offers soil stabilisation against erosion due to its ability to colonize stony and rocky slopes. In its distribution area, ''Q. alnifolia'' is the most important broadleaved species forming pure or mixed stands, within the conifer (''Pinus brutia'', ''[[Pinus nigra]]'') dominated forests of Cyprus. Thick stands of ''Q. alnifolia'' in mesic habitats, considerably modify the humidity conditions of the site and form forest soils with "mull" [[humus]] favouring the existence of sciophilous herbal species.

Like other members of the oak genus, ''Q. alnifolia'' forms mutually beneficial, [[ectomycorrhiza]]l associations with various [[fungi]]. A preliminary study in 2011, reported over 80 mycorrhizal fungi to be associated with the golden oak; the total number, however, is estimated to be much higher.<ref>Loizides, M. (2011). Quercus alnifolia: The indigenous golden oak of Cyprus and its fungi. Field Mycology 12 (3): 81–88. [[doi:10.1016/j.fldmyc.2011.06.004]].</ref>

== Conservation ==
Golden oak is protected by the forest law of Cyprus, while the habitat type "Scrub and low forest vegetation of ''Quercus alnifolia'' (9390)" is a priority habitat of Europe (directive 92/43/EEC).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=CELEX:31992L0043:EN:HTML |title=Council Directive 92/43/EEC of 21 May 1992 on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora |access-date=2008-01-01 |date=1992-07-22 |work=EUR-Lex |publisher=European Union law }}</ref> Large forest expanses of the species have been proposed for inclusion in the [[Natura 2000]] ecological network of the European Union.
